I will keep most of the land in soybean and millet and not spread myself into more crops. I have 220.1 mu, so I need a plan that is stable, mechanized, and not too labor-heavy for a 4-person household. Soybean fits my rotation and input budget better, and millet gives me some diversification in case soybean price or weather goes against me. I have only 5 years of farming experience, so I still lean on what has worked locally, but with my education level I do adjust rates and timing instead of just copying one fixed practice. This year I would put the better, more even fields into soybean because it responds well when the stand is uniform, and keep the drier or lighter fields in millet because it is more tolerant and cheaper to manage. I have well irrigation, but pumping costs money, so I would not irrigate on a calendar unless the soil moisture is clearly short around emergence or flowering.

For soybean, I would use improved seed and keep fertilizer moderate. Soybean does not need heavy nitrogen, so I would mainly support early growth with a small starter N and make sure phosphorus and potassium are there. Weed control matters more than chasing too much fertilizer. For millet, I would use a cleaner seed lot or hybrid seed, put most fertilizer at planting, and leave a small topdress option only if early growth is weak after rain. With 220.1 mu, I would rely on machinery for sowing and most field operations and keep family labor mainly for supervision, irrigation scheduling, and checking pests. My main tradeoff this year is cash versus yield security: I would rather keep input rates at a solid middle level across all fields than push a few fields very hard and leave myself short on cash later.
